newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African firm denies sending mercenaries to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: S.African firm denies sending mercenaries to Zaire.

text.p: South African-based firm Executive Outcomes on Tuesday said it had not sent mercenaries to join a "White Legion" reported assembling in Zaire to help Kinshasa's army stem advances by Rwandan-backed rebels.
Managing director of the Pretoria-based firm, Eeben Barlow, told Reuters:"We've never been in Zaire and we're never been asked by the Zairean authorities to go there."

The Paris daily Le Monde reported that a force of South African, French, Belgian, British, Angolan and Mozambican mercenaries, some recruited by a former chief of security at the French presidency, had gathered in eastern Zaire.
Le Monde said the force numbered between 200 and 300 but was expected to grow rapidly when more men left Europe in two weeks to join the soldiers of fortune on the spot.
The French presidency has denied any connection with or knowledge of the force.

The Le Monde report followed statements in Goma, eastern Zaire, on Monday by Laurent Kabila, head of the rebels, who said 1,000 French soldiers had arrived in Kisangani to help Zairean government forces.
Kabila also alleged there were mercenaries from Executive Outcomes at Watsa, near Kisangani. Barlow denied there was any truth in Kabila's comments.
